issues.t: Head gasket leaks
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, a sweet coolant smell, oil or coolant seeping from the sides of the engine, or the temperature gauge creeping up.
issues.why: The non-turbo 2.5L boxer engine is known for head gasket failures, usually at higher mileage. The earliest engines tended to leak coolant internally, while 2000-2009 engines more often seep oil and coolant on the outside.
issues.next: Have a shop pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the gasket area. If the engine overheats, pull over and shut it off rather than driving on, since overheating can ruin the engine.

issues.t: AWD binding in tight turns (automatic)
issues.sym: In slow, tight turns such as parking lots, the car feels like it is braking itself, hops, or shudders. It drives normally in a straight line.
issues.why: On automatic models the all-wheel-drive transfer clutch, or the solenoid that controls it, can stick so the front and rear wheels are locked together when they should be able to turn at different speeds.
issues.next: Make sure all four tires are the same size and evenly worn, then have a Subaru-savvy shop check the transfer clutch and its solenoid. Ongoing binding wears the drivetrain.

issues.t: Catalytic converter failure (P0420)
issues.sym: Check engine light with a catalyst efficiency code, sometimes a rattle from under the car or a failed emissions test.
issues.why: The catalytic converters on these Outbacks are a frequent failure item, often along with exhaust leaks and loose heat shields. Misfires or oil burning can speed up the damage.
issues.next: Have the code read and the oxygen sensors and exhaust checked for leaks before replacing the converter. Fix any misfire first so the new part is not damaged.

issues.t: Brake lines can rust through (recall)
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, brake fluid dripping near the rear of the car, or longer stopping distances.
issues.why: In states that use road salt, brake lines near the fuel tank protector can corrode and leak fluid. Subaru recalled these cars to inspect and protect or replace the lines.
issues.next: If the pedal feels soft or you see fluid, do not drive the car; have it towed. Check your VIN for open recall work.

issues.t: Secondary air pump can stay on and overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A hot or burning plastic smell from the engine bay, or an air pump that keeps running after start-up.
issues.why: A relay for the secondary air injection pump can stick closed, so the pump runs continuously, overheats, and can melt, creating a fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have it done right away. If you smell burning plastic, park the car away from buildings and have it inspected.

issues.t: CVT cooler hose can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: Transmission fluid on the ground or a burning smell, followed by the car losing drive.
issues.why: A hose for the CVT fluid cooler on early 2010 Outbacks could crack and let the transmission lose its fluid, which can leave the car unable to move.
issues.next: Confirm the recall was done. If you see fluid leaking or the car stops pulling, do not keep driving; have it towed.

issues.t: CVT shudder, jerking, or stalling
issues.sym: Shudder or bucking when pulling away gently, a bump at idle, or the engine nearly stalling as you brake to a stop.
issues.why: Torque converter, sensor and seal problems in early Lineartronic CVTs caused judder, leaks and low-speed stalling. Subaru issued several bulletins and extended CVT coverage on these years.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check for CVT software updates and related bulletins, and whether any extended coverage still applies to your VIN. Keep up with CVT fluid service.

issues.t: Wiper motor cover can overheat and melt (recall)
issues.sym: Wipers slow down or bind, then a burning plastic smell near the base of the windshield.
issues.why: Dirt and debris can make the wipers bind. The motor then overheats and its cover can melt, which risks a fire and leaves you without working wipers.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. If the wipers bind or you smell burning, stop using them and have the car inspected before driving in bad weather.

issues.t: Electronic parking brake may not hold (manual transmission, recall)
issues.sym: The car creeps or rolls after you set the parking brake.
issues.why: On manual-transmission Outbacks the electronic parking brake actuator may not apply as it should, so the car could roll away when parked.
issues.next: Until the recall is done, park in gear with the wheels turned to the curb. Have the actuator replaced under the recall.

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption
issues.sym: The oil level drops well before the next oil change and the low oil light may come on.
issues.why: Piston ring problems on early FB25 engines let some burn oil. The issue led to a class settlement covering these years.
issues.next: Check the dipstick every couple of fill-ups and never let it run low. Ask a dealer for an oil consumption test if it keeps dropping.

issues.t: Steering column shafts may separate (recall)
issues.sym: Steering may feel loose or odd, and in the worst case turning the wheel does not steer the car.
issues.why: Parts of the steering column shaft could come apart, which would mean a loss of steering control.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and get it fixed before regular driving. If the steering feels loose or clunks, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: Battery drains while parked
issues.sym: The car will not start after sitting a day or two, or the battery keeps going weak and needs jump starts.
issues.why: Some electronic modules, including the telematics system, can fail to go to sleep and keep drawing power after shutoff. Subaru issued a bulletin for module reprogramming and settled a class action that extended battery coverage.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested and ask a dealer about module software updates and any extended coverage for your VIN.

issues.t: Windshield cracks with no clear impact
issues.sym: A crack shows up in the windshield without any stone strike, sometimes spreading quickly, and replacements may crack again.
issues.why: Owners widely reported windshields cracking easily on these generations, and a class settlement offered reimbursement and extended coverage for some model years.
issues.next: Have cracks in the driver's view repaired promptly since they can affect visibility and driver-assist cameras. Ask a dealer whether settlement coverage applies.

issues.t: Touchscreen radio freezes or glitches
issues.sym: The radio or navigation screen freezes, stops responding, or loses phone connection.
issues.why: The infotainment head unit on this generation is known for software glitches that lock up the screen.
issues.next: Restart the car to reset the screen, then ask a dealer to load the latest head unit software.

issues.t: Transmission oil can leak onto exhaust (recall)
issues.sym: A burning oil smell or smoke from under the car, or drips near the middle of the car.
issues.why: On some mid-2015 builds, a seal cap on the propeller shaft could be deformed, letting transmission oil leak onto the hot exhaust and creating a fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. If you smell burning oil or see smoke, pull over, shut the engine off and have the car towed.

issues.t: Steering column may be machined wrong (do-not-drive recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning; steering input could stop turning the wheels.
issues.why: Some steering columns were machined incorrectly at the factory, so the steering might not work. Subaru told affected owners not to drive until the repair is done.
issues.next: Check your VIN right away. If it is affected and not yet repaired, do not drive it; have the dealer inspect and replace the column.

issues.t: Low-fuel warning light may not come on (recall)
issues.sym: The car runs out of gas without the low-fuel light ever coming on.
issues.why: A software error can keep the low-fuel warning from lighting, so the car may run dry and stall in traffic.
issues.next: Watch the fuel gauge and refill early until the dealer updates the software under the recall.

issues.t: Low-pressure fuel pump may fail (recall)
issues.sym: Rough running, check engine light, then the engine stalls and may not restart.
issues.why: The in-tank fuel pump uses an impeller that can deform and stop the pump, cutting fuel to the engine while driving.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open fuel pump recalls and get the pump replaced. If the engine stumbles or stalls, get off the road safely and have it towed.

issues.t: Body spot welds below the cowl may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom a driver would notice; it is found by inspection.
issues.why: Some spot welds under the cowl panel may not have been applied correctly, weakening the body structure and crash protection.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have the dealer inspect and repair the car.

issues.t: CVT drive chain can slip and break (recall)
issues.sym: A sudden loss of power or the car will not move, sometimes with warning lights.
issues.why: A software error could let the CVT clutch engage before the drive chain is clamped tightly, so the chain slips and can break.
issues.next: Check your VIN and get the software update. If the car loses drive, get off the road safely and have it towed.

issues.t: Brake pedal bracket bolt may be loose or missing (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal may feel loose or braking may feel weaker than normal.
issues.why: A bolt that holds the brake pedal bracket may have been left loose or out at the factory, which can reduce braking.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. If the pedal feels loose or braking is weak, do not drive until it is inspected.

issues.t: Rearview camera image may drop out (recall)
issues.sym: The backup camera picture goes blank or cuts out while reversing.
issues.why: A failed software update on the cockpit control module could make the rear camera image drop intermittently.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall; the dealer reprograms the software or replaces the module. Use mirrors and look back until it is fixed.

issues.t: Thermo control valve fault
issues.sym: Check engine light, sometimes with temperature or heater changes.
issues.why: The electronic valve that manages coolant flow can suffer sensor corrosion and set fault codes. Subaru released a redesigned valve through a service bulletin.
issues.next: Have the codes read. If they point to the thermo control valve, ask a dealer about the updated part and watch the temperature gauge in the meantime.

issues.t: Passenger occupant sensor may shut off airbag (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag OFF light shows with an adult in the seat, or an airbag warning light comes on.
issues.why: A capacitor in the front passenger occupant sensor can crack and short, so the system may switch off the passenger airbag.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and get the sensor replaced. Until then, avoid seating an adult passenger up front if the airbag OFF light is on.

issues.t: Large touchscreen freezes, blanks or reboots
issues.sym: The tall center screen goes black, freezes or restarts, taking climate controls, audio or the camera view with it for a while.
issues.why: The infotainment system in this generation had software bugs that Subaru has addressed with updates.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to install the latest infotainment software and report repeat failures so they are documented.

issues.t: Gear selector cable nut may loosen (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter may not match the gear the car is actually in, or the car may not go into Park properly.
issues.why: A nut on the CVT select lever cable may not have been tightened, so the gear selector can stop working correctly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Always set the parking brake when parking until it is inspected.

issues.t: Water in inhibitor switch disables reverse lights and camera (recall)
issues.sym: The reverse lights and backup camera stop working, sometimes with a warning light.
issues.why: A weld flaw can let water into the transmission range (inhibitor) switch, which then stops signaling reverse.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Back up with extra care using mirrors until it is repaired.

issues.t: Front coil spring can rust through and break (recall)
issues.sym: A bang or clunk from a front corner, the car sitting lower on one side, or a rubbing noise from a front tire.
issues.why: Thin paint lets the front coil springs corrode. A broken spring can slip past its seat and press against the tire, which can cut it.
issues.next: Have the front springs inspected now. The dealer fits spring guards and replaces broken springs free under the recall.

issues.t: Front suspension bracket welds can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Vague or wandering steering, clunks over bumps, or the car pulling to one side.
issues.why: The bracket that holds the front of the lower suspension arm was not welded properly on some cars and can crack or come away.
issues.next: Have the brackets inspected before driving further. They are replaced free under the recall if they are affected.

issues.t: Shift lever can break or let the car move unexpectedly (recall)
issues.sym: The ignition key sticks, the shifter feels loose or sloppy, or the lever moves out of Park without the brake pedal.
issues.why: Poor welds in the automatic shift lever and its linkage let parts break, so the lever can move or no longer match the gear the car is in.
issues.next: Set the parking brake and have it inspected right away. The dealer replaces the shift lever assembly free under the recall.

issues.t: Throttle may not return fully (recall)
issues.sym: Idle that creeps up and stays high, or the engine not settling back down when you lift off the pedal.
issues.why: A ball bearing was left out of the throttle shaft on some throttle bodies, so over time the shaft binds and the throttle does not close all the way.
issues.next: Have the throttle body inspected before driving much further. The dealer replaces it free under the recall if the bearing is missing.

issues.t: Driveshaft center support bolts can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or vibration from under the middle of the car that gets worse as you drive, sometimes a scraping noise.
issues.why: The bolts holding the driveshaft centre support can work loose, and the front of the shaft can then come away from the car.
issues.next: Stop driving and have it inspected. The dealer cleans the mounting surfaces and fits new bolts free under the recall.
